Vivek Saraswat, Andrew Pieper, Edwin Vázquez-Rosa, Sarah Barker 
Case Western Reserve University, Psychiatry, Cleveland, United States of America 

Aims: To investigate the role of acetylated tau (ac-tau) in traumatic brain injury–accelerated 
Alzheimer’s disease (TBI-AD) and evaluate therapeutic strategies targeting tau acetylation as a means 
to prevent neurodegeneration. 

Methods: 1. Established a TBI-AD model using amyloid-driven 5xFAD mice. 2. Assessed cognitive 
function, microglial activation, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) integrity following TBI. 3. Tested two ac-
tau–lowering interventions: diflunisal (p300/CBP inhibition) and P7C3-A20 (NAD⁺ restoration/Sirt1 
activation). 4. Analyzed clinical data from TBI patients prescribed NSAIDs with or without p300/CBP 
inhibitory activity. 

Results: TBI selectively induced ac-tau in 5xFAD mice, causing cognitive decline, microglial 
activation, and BBB dysfunction. Both diflunisal and P7C3-A20 normalized ac-tau, preventing 
neurodegeneration and restoring BBB integrity. Clinical data showed reduced dementia incidence in 
TBI patients prescribed p300/CBP-inhibiting NSAIDs compared to non-targeting NSAIDs. 

Conclusions: Acetylated tau is a central driver of TBI-AD and a tractable therapeutic target. Dual-
pathway interventions demonstrate that reducing tau acetylation, rather than targeting amyloid, 
effectively prevents TBI-AD progression. Conserved microglial signatures link tau pathology to 
neuroimmune dysfunction and provide translational readouts. These findings support both 
repurposing existing NSAIDs and developing next-generation ac-tau modulators as disease-modifying 
strategies for TBI-accelerated dementia.

title: CHOLINE ALPHOSCERATE IN THE THERAPY OF MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND ASSOCIATED
content:
POSTER ON BOARD SHIFT 02 - BOARD #709  
ABSTRACT SUBMISSION #1930 

CHOLINE ALPHOSCERATE IN THE THERAPY OF MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND ASSOCIATED 
VASCULAR DAMAGE. ONE-YEAR RESULTS OF THE CARL STUDY 

POSTER ON BOARD - SHIFT 02: VASCULAR DISEASES / IMAGING, BIOMARKERS, DIAGNOSTICS 

Enea Traini1, Anna Carotenuto2, Mohammed Hossein1, Vincenzo Andreone2, Francesco Amenta1 
1University of Camerino, School Of Pharmacy, Camerino, Italy, 2A. Cardarelli Hospital, Neurology And 
Stroke Unit-neurology, Naples, Italy 

Aims: Brain atrophy, mainly involving the hippocampus, is related to progression of cognitive 
impairment and conversion from mild cognitive dysfunction to overt dementia. Choline alphoscerate 
is a cholinergic precursor officially approved for the treatment of degenerative-involutive and 
cerebrovascular psychogenic syndromes characterized by age-related memory deficits, confusion, 
reduced motivation, attentional decline, affective instability and behavioral disturbances. 

Methods: The CARL (Choline Alphoscerate in Mild Cognitive Impairment) study evaluated the efficacy 
of choline alphoscerate in patients with MCI and associated vascular damage, in slowing the 
hippocampal, entorhinal, cortical atrophy, the ventricular dilation and the progression of cognitive 
and behavioural symptoms associated with MCI and concomitant vascular brain injury. In this double-
blind, placebo-controlled trial, 60 elderly MCI subjects (exhibiting MRI evidence of vascular-related 
brain changes) were randomized 1:1 to receive either choline alphoscerate 1,200 mg/day or placebo. 
High-resolution T1-weighted MRI scans were acquired and analyzed at the baseline and after 12-
month; hippocampal, entorhinal, neocortical volumes and ventricular dimensions were quantified 
using FreeSurfer v7.4.1. Cognitive, functional and behavioural status were evaluated by a 
comprehensive neuropsychological battery at study entry and during one year of follow-up. 

Results: The hippocampal region shows signs of degeneration before the onset of cognitive 
symptoms and represents the first region to degenerate. After one year, patients treated with choline 
alphoscerate demonstrated a significantly lower rate of hippocampal and entorhinal atrophy, and less 
ventricular dilation, compared with placebo. Neuropsychological evaluation showed a relevant 
difference between the two groups mainly in behavioral tests with a significative reduction in apathy in 
the choline alphoscerate treated group. 

Conclusions: These findings reinforce the efficacy of choline alphoscerate in improving behavioural 
symptoms and reveal a significant efficacy in attenuating the progression of early neurodegenerative 
changes in MCI with vascular involvement.
